text: Peace be upon you and God's mercy. Look, everyone, you know that I rarely come out to talk about something,
but I feel that I am carrying a responsibility, and I owe it to you to tell you about my experience
with this subject, very briefly. I am going to talk about something that happened to me about two years ago.
It was a serious health problem. What happened was that I had slipped discs
in four vertebrae, and the situation looked frightening. When I had
an MRI, the result was truly frightening, to the point that I was not allowed to carry Yasmina.
It was completely forbidden. The doctor told me literally that, by God's grace, there were only about two millimeters
between the disc and the nerve; otherwise I would have needed surgery immediately. This is the first time I am saying this publicly, although people close to me knew
these details very well. I am not someone who likes to publicize that I am sick or
seek attention because of it. On the contrary, I used to withdraw and disappear, and people did not know why. That is just my nature.
Anyway, purely by coincidence, a friend of mine called me. Her condition was very serious.
She had cancer, and the doctors had almost lost hope because it had spread extensively through her body.
At one point she even traveled abroad with her husband for treatment, but she returned still struggling.
She had taken many medications and undergone chemotherapy. Fortunately, she was from Cairo,
and after a lot of effort she managed to reach Dr. Diaa Al-Awady. She met him, and he
gave her a regimen that she described as simple yet powerful—something inexpensive and not complicated at all.
She felt it made an enormous difference for her. She followed the regimen without telling anyone, and suddenly I found her calling me

on the phone saying she wanted to tell me something good. She said, 'Do you remember that doctor?' I told her, 'Please, not him—the man who keeps saying things like if your wife yells at you, divorce her.'
I thought he sounded completely crazy. She told me, 'Forget all that. Put it aside and focus on what is useful.' I asked her what she meant.
She said, 'Thank God, I feel that God has healed me.' I said, 'God has healed you? Mashallah, there is no power except through God—how?'
She said, 'I followed the Al-Tayyibat system.' I asked, 'What is the Al-Tayyibat system?' Then she began
to explain the whole story to me. She said, 'Fast until you genuinely feel hungry. If you are hungry, eat. If you want to
sleep, sleep. It does not have to be eight hours. Nothing is rigid. Drink when you are thirsty.'
She said, 'You are not connected to a hose drinking water constantly. If you are thirsty, drink. If you are hungry, eat.' I asked what kind of food plan it was and whether it was difficult.
She told me, 'No, not at all. There are only about five basic things to follow.' Then she started
explaining the system to me, and I thought to myself that I was already in a difficult position anyway.
Either way, I felt heavily restricted. The doctors had told me 'no' to so many things that life had become dark for me.
I was exhausted and felt sorry for myself, and I did not even know how to complain because complaining is not my nature.
Eventually I became so frustrated that I said, 'I will try it. Even if I make one step forward, that is still a gain.'
God willing, I thought, I might feel some improvement. So I started, and what happened was this:
First, thank God, I returned to exercising. I went back to swimming and started doing the things
I wanted to do. My movement changed completely, thank God. I felt as though I had gone back
at least 20 or 25 years in terms of how healthy and active I felt. I attribute that to God's grace.
Sometimes I even tell myself that I am afraid of envying myself because I truly feel that so many of the things
that had worried me, and made me think I was becoming almost disabled, had changed. [laughs]
I wanted to share this information with you, everyone.
From my point of view, if this man were simply saying nonsense, why would there be so much opposition to him?
Especially, in her view, from pharmaceutical companies and poultry producers. She says she stopped everything Dr. Diaa Al-Awady considered harmful.
She says she followed his theory as he explained it and watched his videos closely.
She describes listening to them with great seriousness, to understand what he recommended and what he advised avoiding.
She says his basic list was simple and inexpensive: dates, rice, oil, sugar, and potatoes.
She says he did not recommend meat often—only about once a week—and fish about once
a week. She describes fasting until real hunger appears, then eating when hungry.
She says she dropped two clothing sizes, which she considered a major improvement for herself.
She also says her body felt lighter, and she repeatedly expresses gratitude to God for how she felt.
She says she could never fully repay what she sees as God's blessing, even if she spent her whole life in gratitude.
Her message is that someone with an existing health problem may feel they have little to lose by trying something new.
She says, 'I already had a health problem, so I thought: why not try? What would I lose?'
She suggests trying it for three days and, in her view, continuing only if one personally feels progress.
She says that if there is improvement, continue for another three days, and then another three days.
Then she adds another personal lesson from her own experience that she hopes others will consider:
seek God's satisfaction, and then take care of your own well-being.
She says that things that only bring you distress are often not worth carrying, because the person upsetting you may be happy an hour later
while you remain sick, exhausted, and carrying a burden that was never really yours.
She asks: why carry it? Life is short, and if you do not value yourself, others may not value you either.
She concludes by saying that she has delivered her message and asks God to be witness to it, then entrusts everyone to God's care.
She ends the recording.
